HUB_POOL_SECTION_DESC: Pool inference capacity with other CI-Hub devices on your tailnet. Once a peer is connected, apps route through whichever paired Hub currently has the model.
HUB_POOL_DISCOVERABLE_EMPTY: No unpaired CI-Hub devices found. Check that the other Hub is running and connected to Tailscale. A Hub that no directory here names can still be paired with from the CLI, by address and a PIN: cihub pool pair <address> --pin <digits>. Both Hubs have to be on the same tailnet either way, because a peer is stored under its tailnet name.
HUB_POOL_PEER_ENABLED: Peer is back in the pool.
HUB_POOL_PEER_DISABLED: Peer taken out of the pool. The pairing is kept.
HUB_POOL_PEER_TOGGLE_ERROR: Failed to change this peer's pooling.
HUB_POOL_REASON_ACTIVE: Apps on this Hub are being routed through the pool. Each request goes to whichever paired Hub has the model and the shortest queue.
HUB_POOL_REASON_NO_PEERS: Pooling is on, but no Hub is paired yet, so every request is served by this node's own engines. Pair a Hub below to start sharing capacity.
HUB_POOL_REASON_DISABLED_SETTING: Pooling is turned off on this Hub. Apps only use local engines, and paired Hubs treat this node as unavailable. Pairings are kept — turn it back on below.
HUB_POOL_REASON_DISABLED_ENV: Pooling is turned off for this appliance by HUB_POOL_USER_DISABLED in its .env file.
HUB_POOL_REASON_PARTIAL: Pooling is on, but only part of it is running — one direction is switched off, or every paired Hub is individually disabled. Check the controls below.
HUB_POOL_ENV_LOCK_HINT: The environment flag wins over the toggle below, so switching it here would change nothing. Remove HUB_POOL_USER_DISABLED=true from the Hub's .env and restart to make pooling controllable from this page.
HUB_POOL_QUEUE_HINT: In-flight counts are live gauges measured by this Hub since it last started, not request totals.
HUB_POOL_LOCAL_CAPABILITIES_ERROR: This Hub could not reach its own inference engines ({{error}}), so its model list is unknown rather than empty.
HUB_POOL_TAILSCALE_OFFLINE: Tailscale is not connected on this Hub, so no peer can reach it and pooling cannot route anywhere. Connect it in Private VPN above.
HUB_POOL_TOGGLE_HELP: On: apps here can be served by any paired Hub, and this Hub serves theirs. Off: every request stays on local hardware and paired Hubs skip this node. Pairings are kept either way, so turning it back on needs no re-approval.
HUB_POOL_TOGGLE_ENV_LOCKED: Locked off by HUB_POOL_USER_DISABLED in this Hub's .env — this toggle cannot override it.
HUB_POOL_OUTBOUND_HELP: On: a request can be served by whichever paired Hub is least busy. Off: every request stays on this node's own engines, and one it cannot serve fails here instead of being sent out. Pairings and health checks are kept.
HUB_POOL_OUTBOUND_ENV_LOCKED: Locked off by HUB_POOL_OUTBOUND_DISABLED in this Hub's .env — this toggle cannot override it.
HUB_POOL_INBOUND_HELP: On: paired Hubs may run their requests on this node's engines. Off: they see this Hub as healthy but not taking work, and route elsewhere — this Hub keeps using them. Pairings are kept either way.
HUB_POOL_INBOUND_ENV_LOCKED: Locked off by HUB_POOL_INBOUND_DISABLED in this Hub's .env — this toggle cannot override it.
HUB_POOL_AFFINITY_HELP: The head start this Hub gives itself before handing work to a peer. Higher keeps a conversation on one node so its prompt cache is reused; 0 spreads work by whoever is least busy — this Hub still takes an exact tie, since serving here costs no hop — at the cost of re-reading the prompt on the new node.
HUB_POOL_POLL_HELP: How often each paired Hub is probed. Longer means less tailnet traffic but slower reaction to a Hub going down — three missed probes in a row mark a peer unreachable.
HUB_POOL_CONNECTED_HELP: Hubs this node can send work to, and that can send work here.
HUB_POOL_UNREACHABLE_HINT: The last {{failures}} health checks failed, so this Hub is skipped when routing. It rejoins the pool by itself on the next successful check — there is no need to unpair it.
HUB_POOL_MODELS_HELP: Models reported by every reachable Hub, with the nodes that currently have each one. This is the capacity pooling added to this Hub.
HUB_POOL_MODELS_EMPTY: No node in the pool has reported a model yet.
HUB_POOL_ROUTING_HELP: Where recent requests were served, newest first. Kept in memory only, so restarting the Hub clears it — an empty list means nothing has been routed since the last restart.
HUB_POOL_ROUTING_EMPTY: Nothing has been routed since this Hub started.
HUB_POOL_DISCOVERABLE_HELP: CI-Hub devices this Hub can name and has not paired with yet, from your tailnet and from the Hubs registered to your CI account.
HUB_POOL_DISCOVERY_UNCONFIGURED_SHORT: No tailnet-wide directory — showing only what this Hub's own Tailscale daemon can see.
HUB_POOL_DISCOVERY_UNCONFIGURED: This Hub has no Tailscale API credential, so it cannot list your whole tailnet at once. Discovery still asks the peers this Hub's own Tailscale daemon can see when it is connected to a tailnet, and the Hubs on your CI account when this Hub is registered to one — neither of those needs a credential. To enumerate the tailnet, set TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET in the Hub's .env and restart. The credential is not needed to be paired with: another Hub's request appears below.
HUB_POOL_PENDING_HELP: Pairing is two-way: approve a request here, and the other Hub approves yours.
HUB_POOL_CANCEL_REQUEST_ERROR: Failed to cancel the pairing request.
HUB_POOL_UNPAIR_CONFIRM: Unpair {{name}}? This deletes the pairing and revokes both Hubs’ tokens, so neither node can route to the other until you pair again and the other Hub approves.
HUB_POOL_STATUS_ERROR: Could not load the Hub Pool status. This page retries every 15 seconds; pooling itself keeps running either way.
HUB_POOL_PIN_HELP: Generate a PIN here, then type it into the other Hub while pairing. A PIN authenticates the pairing request itself, so a request that arrives without one — or with a wrong one — creates nothing. You still confirm the peer below before any work is exchanged.
HUB_POOL_PIN_ACTIVE_ELSEWHERE: A pairing PIN is outstanding. The digits are shown only once, when it is generated — generate a new one to see a code.
HUB_POOL_PIN_MINT_ERROR: Could not generate a pairing PIN
HUB_POOL_PIN_CANCEL_ERROR: Could not cancel the pairing PIN
HUB_POOL_IDENTITY_ERROR: This node cannot sign pool requests and is using its pairing tokens instead: {{error}}
HUB_POOL_PEER_FINGERPRINT_UNVERIFIED: No key — this request arrived without a pairing PIN, so the name is only a claim.
HUB_POOL_PEER_BEARER_HELP: This peer still authenticates with the original bearer token rather than a pinned key. The upgrade happens on its own at the next health poll. Do not turn on poolRequireSignedPeers while any peer is in this state — it would cut them off in both directions.
HUB_POOL_PINS_HELP: Prefer one node for a model, or for everything. A pin only moves that node to the front of the candidates — if it cannot serve a request the pool ranks normally, so a pin can never take inference down.
HUB_POOL_PINS_EMPTY: No pins. Requests go to whichever node has the model and the shortest queue.
HUB_POOL_PINS_UNPAIRED: A Hub that is no longer paired
HUB_POOL_PINS_SAVED: Pin saved — it applies to the next request.
HUB_POOL_UNPAIR_CONFIRM_PINS: A routing pin points at this peer. It is left in place and simply stops applying — remove it under Routing pins.
